change.title: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader
change.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/db/migrations/0042_reader_shard_grants.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- Make the reader's access to shard databases explicit so per-principal
+-- query limits and audit logging apply to it.
+GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader;

verdict.headline: Explicit shard grants double svc_bundle_reader's visible rows from 99 to 198, approaching worker-runtime max_entries=200 limit at 99% capacity
verdict.cause: The change adds GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader, expanding the reader's table access from the default schema to all tables in database r0. Experiment comparison shows: baseline loaded_entries=99 → candidate loaded_entries=198 (2x increase). worker-runtime max_entries=200 (row_id: w-h9c5/setting/worker-runtime.max_entries). The 198 loaded entries operate at 99% of the 200-entry limit, leaving only 2 entries of headroom. The meta-store rows_visible_to_builder also doubled from 99 to 198, confirming the grant expanded query scope. While 198 < 200 technically stays under the limit, the proximity is concerning.
tested: x-251aab3cdabc49ef: baseline · workload default → all assertions passed
x-f40892ba060344c6: candidate · workload default → all assertions passed
x-1833518d0388442b: control · workload default → all assertions passed
limitations:
- Only one workload (default) tested; other workloads may have different query patterns
- No testing of per-principal query limit enforcement mechanics
- No audit logging behavior observed under the change
- Only 288 runs observed over 7 days; longer-term patterns unknown
Baseline and candidate both passed under every tested workload.

causal_chain.edge: h1: The change adds GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader in addition to existing grants, expanding the reader's table access from implicit/default scope to all tables in database r0. This causes bundle-builder query q-bundle-fields to scan more tables, doubling rows_returned_p50 from 99 to 198.
